title: cAtari: Continuum's own Atari 7800 emulator, replacing ProSystem (owner, 27 October 2026: 'Then do the Atari 7800.')
why: The owner's order of 25 October: after cBoy and cGear, build the next easiest core, as good as the outside emulator it replaces and with more settings. Asked which is next easiest, the answer was Pokemon Mini first and the Atari 7800 a close second with better value (our own 6502 then serves the 2600, 5200, Lynx, NES and PC Engine); the owner chose the 7800, and had subagents start the Pokemon Mini (cMini, tasks/pokemini.json, in its own clone /projects/sandbox/.scratch/pokemini-work) at the same time.
names: App name cAtari (working name; the owner can rename it). Crate cores/continuum-atari, crate continuum_atari, core id continuum_atari, library continuum_atari_libretro_ios.dylib, option prefix catari_. The name covers more than the 7800 on purpose: the real 7800 plays 2600 cartridges, and the same 6502 is the start of the other Atari consoles.
rules: Our own Rust, GPL-3.0-only like cBoy, cGear and cArcade. Read Atari's documents, the chips' data sheets and how MAME 0.289's a7800 driver and ProSystem behave; never copy code.

NEVER fetch or commit a commercial ROM or the 7800 BIOS. Test with SingleStepTests, Klaus Dormann's test, and our own programs (assembled in scratch), openly licensed homebrew only, fetched into scratch.
The game starts straight away with no BIOS (ProSystem does too). The player's own 7800 BIOS, when it is in the system folder, can play its Atari logo first (a setting). No made-up startup picture.
In the app it is a second choice next to ProSystem (ProSystem stays the default until the owner has seen cAtari work on his phone).
Push to master after every green piece, every commit [skip ci]; ONE build when cAtari and cMini are both done. Never edit native/ios/build-engine.sh or .github/workflows/.
Green before every push: cargo test --release in cores/continuum-atari; when touching the app wiring, the checks in HANDOFF.md 'How to check work before pushing'.

Reference MAME: /projects/sandbox/.scratch/mame/mame-mame0289/arcaderef (has a7800 and a7800p since 27 October; .kiro/notes/wip/tools/mame-READY.txt). Its a7800 needs a BIOS file: give it our own stand-in.

items.title: The 6502 (Atari's SALLY), every bus cycle
items.result: src/m6502.rs: every opcode including the undocumented ones and decimal mode, each cycle's read or write in the chip's order, NMI and IRQ polled where the real chip polls them. All 2,560,000 SingleStepTests cases match cycle for cycle (tests/m6502_singlestep.rs) and Klaus Dormann's functional test passes (tests/m6502_functional.rs).

items.title: Settings inventory
items.detail: Every setting of ProSystem (libretro, the app's current core), a7800 (the standalone, MAME-based), MAME's a7800, BizHawk's A7800Hawk, js7800 and EMU7800, generated as CORE_OPTIONS_STANDARD.md says, in .kiro/notes/docs/A7800_OPTIONS_INVENTORY.md; each planned, app or n/a.
items.result: .kiro/notes/docs/A7800_OPTIONS_INVENTORY.md: ProSystem's 4 settings, MAME 0.289's and a7800's (difficulty switches, BIOS, palettes, HSC, controllers, XM), BizHawk's, JS7800's and EMU7800's, each done, app or n/a; gaps: rare controllers (the XM and the Souper music player are done).

items.title: The 7800 itself
items.detail: Memory map and mirrors, the slow cycles for TIA and RIOT, INPTCTRL and its lock, the BIOS when there is one, the RIOT (timers, ports, RAM), the TIA (sound, buttons, paddles), MARIA (DMA with its cycle costs halting the processor, the display list list and display lists, all six read modes, holey DMA, character mode, kangaroo mode, the DLI's NMI, WSYNC), NTSC and PAL, the palettes.
items.result: src/machine.rs (memory map, MARIA's DMA holding the processor, WSYNC, the slow TIA/RIOT cycles as a setting, INPTCTRL and its lock, the BIOS when there is one), maria.rs (display lists, all read modes, holey DMA, kangaroo, display list interrupts), tia.rs (sound, buttons, paddles), riot.rs (timers as Stella measures them, ports), pokey.rs (all four channels, the polynomials, both clocks, joined channels, high-pass filters, two-tone and asynchronous modes; its interrupt not wired, as on MAME, a7800 and ProSystem). The console starts in the line after the picture, as MAME's does. Proofs in A7.

items.title: Cartridges
items.detail: .a78 headers (v1 to v4), headerless .bin, every bank-switching scheme ProSystem and a7800 play (SuperGame with its RAM and bank-6 variants, Absolute, Activision, Souper, BankSet), POKEY on the cartridge, cartridge RAM, the High Score Cartridge (the player's own HSC file), SaveKey/AtariVox saves.
items.result: Done: .a78 headers (the v4 bits), headerless files by MAME's CC0 list (189), every board MAME 0.289 plays, plus BankSet (all variants, as the a7800 emulator plays them), the Souper board (as ProSystem), POKEY at $0440/$0450/$0800 as well as $4000, 52 KB BankSet images from $3000, the High Score Cartridge (the player's own highscre.bin, a setting: Auto/Every game/Off; proved against MAME), SaveKey/AtariVox (32 KB EEPROM on port 2, by the 24LC256 data sheet; Auto for games whose header asks). Battery memory (HSC RAM, SaveKey) is the core's save RAM. The XM expansion module and the XBoarD too (src/xm.rs: 128 KB of RAM in 8 KB pages, the processor and MARIA each with their own pages, its POKEY at $0450, its YM2151 FM chip at $0460 (src/ym2151.rs, our own, matching MAME 0.289 sample for sample), its High Score part, the five control registers as the a7800 emulator and the community document them; a setting catari_xm Auto/Every game/Off, Auto from the header). The Souper board's music player too (src/coretone.rs, src/bupchip.rs: the BupChip that plays Rikki & Vikki's music from the files its .cdf names, CoreTone 1.2.2cz translated to Rust under its zlib licence, notice kept and marked altered; matching the original sample for sample, 520,000 samples, tests/coretone.rs; a setting catari_bupchip_volume; the app imports .smp/.ins/.mus and the core finds them side by side).

items.title: Controls
items.detail: Two-button ProLine joysticks and one-button 2600 joysticks, Pause, Select, Reset and the two difficulty switches, the light gun games, paddles.
items.result: Two-button and one-button joysticks, Pause/Select/Reset and both difficulty switches (proved against MAME, tests/references/inputs.txt), the light gun (sensor on INPT4, trigger on the stick's up line, as the a7800 emulator models it), paddles (VBLANK bit 7 dumps the capacitors), SaveKey/AtariVox on port 2; pad mapping as ProSystem's so the app's touch layout fits. The app now maps a tap through the renderer's exact visible-picture placement, so bars cannot begin a shot. The cAtari app path is proved by the FEAT-002 scratch pointer probe; a real light-gun game remains a phone check.

items.title: The libretro core
items.detail: Entry points, settings (catari_), save states, memory for cheats and RetroAchievements, battery saves, picture, sound.
items.result: src/libretro.rs and src/options.rs: the entry points, 25 settings (catari_), save states that keep the RAM where the app was told it is, reset, the memory map for achievements and 4 KB of RAM for cheats; tests/libretro.rs plays the test game through them (picture, 48 kHz sound to the sample, save state, reset, live colour change).

items.title: Proved against MAME 0.289
items.detail: Our own 7800 test programs run on cAtari and MAME's a7800: the processor's trace, every frame, the sound; pinned in tests/references so the tests run without MAME.
items.result: Matched against MAME 0.289 (tests/mame_frames.rs, tia_mame.rs, pokey_mame.rs; references by tests/mame/make_refs.py, nothing of MAME's committed): zones 120 frames, dma 60, modes 70, inputs 110, five bank boards 20 each, the High Score Cartridge 12, and on the PAL console zones 60 and every read mode 70, dot for dot; the TIA's sound, all 204,800 samples; POKEY's sound, every one of 6.2 million clocks through MAME's recording (3.1 million samples, none more than 8 out of 32,768), with MAME's clock rounding and its 50-a-second sound updates allowed for; the XM's YM2151, all 223,878 samples of a test playing every connection, the LFO's four waveforms, the noise and the envelopes (tests/ym2151_mame.rs), with MAME's rounded sample rate and its processor's cycle phase after a WSYNC allowed for. The RIOT against Stella (tests/riot_stella.rs). Not compared (no reference emulator in hand): BankSet, Souper, POKEY at $0440/$0800, the XM's RAM paging (MAME's XM is a rougher stand-in with one 16 KB window; ours follows the a7800 emulator's documented registers), SaveKey (unit tests from the reference emulators' behaviour and the EEPROM's data sheet).

items.title: In the app
items.detail: Second choice next to ProSystem: CoreSpec, coreChoices, build-core.sh recipe, project.yml, not-in-ios-yml.txt, check-core-cache.sh, engine frontend test, touch controls.
items.result: Second choice for the 7800 next to ProSystem (ContinuumApp.swift CoreSpec continuumAtari, coreChoices[.atari7800], its picture shape from the core), its own regions in scripts/build-core.sh, project.yml, not-in-ios-yml.txt, check-core-cache.sh (229 checks pass); crates/emulator-bridge/tests/catari_frontend.rs opens it through the app engine. The app touch layout keeps the ProSystem button mapping and adds renderer-owned whole-picture pointer mapping for cAtari's light gun. ProSystem remains first/default.
